## 3. Selected producer interface and layout — required design, not existing fact

Create the narrowly named canonical entry point `scripts/kaola-workflow-keep-open-project.js`. Its supported install operation is:

```text
node <accepted-producer>/scripts/kaola-workflow-keep-open-project.js install \
  --target /Users/ylmacstudio/Workspace/vrpcadcore \
  --project issue-143 --issue 143 \
  --claim-digest 013df64014a5a5354b9796879f1574260b6cb346fec9007586779cb2cf69573b \
  --source-commit <full-accepted-C> --acceptance <Host-accepted-receipt>
```

This spelling is the selected interface to implement and document, not a command to try today. It is GitHub/Codex/explicit-singleton-only. No runtime enumeration, marketplace commands, auto-update, arbitrary plugin installation, global mode, default activation or automatic dependency download belongs in it. `inspect --manifest <absolute-path>` reports identity, paths, completeness and incompatibilities without running workflow code. `remove --manifest <absolute-path>` is ownership-checked local bundle removal subject to the rollback limits below. Do not call the existing Codex hook/profile installer internally.

Use one immutable directory:

```text
<consumer-MAIN>/.kw/provider-adoptions/issue-143/<full-C>/
  adoption.json
  plugins/kaola-workflow/
    .codex-plugin/plugin.json
    skills/kaola-workflow-finalize/SKILL.md
    skills/kaola-workflow-next/SKILL.md
    scripts/<declared complete runtime helper closure>
```

This preserves the existing plugin's caller/helper layout inside a private project scope. It is **not** a native Codex plugin registration, not a second marketplace, and not a new search root automatically inserted into normal resolution. No new `commands/` directory is invented. Do not populate MAIN or a linked worktree's ordinary `plugins/kaola-workflow`, install duplicate named skills into discovery directories, create a producer-worktree symlink, or modify an installed skill by hand. The installer derives the payload from exact committed producer bytes and its source-owned materialization manifest. Path-specific caller binding, if required, is a deterministic render whose template hash, parameters and rendered hash are recorded; it is not post-install text editing.

`adoption.json` records schema, capability `github-explicit-singleton-keep-open-pr`, runtime/forge, source repository/commit/tree, actual package/plugin version, complete relative file list with sizes/modes/SHA-256 and source blobs, generated-caller provenance, canonical target MAIN and Git common-directory identity, consumer repository/claim/project/issue/branch/worktree binding, original state/ledger identities, acceptance receipt references/hashes, and the supported state/receipt contract. It records observations, not a fabricated permission token or a QA verdict inferred from an exit code. Manifest paths must be derived and confined, never blindly trusted for writes/deletion. Full source commit and hashes supplement the unchanged real version; no fake version or compatibility bypass.

Preflight all destinations and symlink ancestors. Refuse foreign ownership, path traversal, changed existing files, source/candidate disagreement, wrong repository/claim, unexpected extra executable files or incomplete closure. Stage inside this one project namespace, hash-verify, then atomically publish only a complete new directory. Same C and same bytes is idempotent. A failed transaction leaves the former usable bundle untouched and cannot register partial content. Do not touch Git index, refs, config, ignore files, hooks or lifecycle state. Establish that the chosen namespace is already safely local/ignored before installation; if not, report that concrete prerequisite instead of silently editing ignore policy. A returned inspection receipt is not activation or publication.

## 4. Matched caller, resolver and recovery contract

Host must explicitly read the installed bundle's **complete generated Finalization caller by absolute path**, verify its manifest/caller hash, and select that manifest for this operation. The producer must document this supported invocation. Reading a local caller is not assumed to register a native skill or hot-reload a stale conversation. The global caller `28a53fe8` is insufficient even when a sink file is new.

Author an explicit scope branch in the GitHub Codex routing resolver. A scoped caller supplies the exact manifest and expected identity; the resolver validates it and yields one absolute `CLAIM_JS` plus one absolute `KAOLA_SCRIPTS` from that bundle. Resolve once per invocation, and carry the same checked identity into every downstream entry, including after `cd` into the linked worktree. The new explicit binding must be passed by the generated invocation, not exported into a shell startup file or silently inherited as a global setting. When no scope was explicitly selected, retain the current project-first/global-fallback resolver and behavior unchanged. When a scope was selected but is invalid, **refuse; never fall back** to global, `~/.agents`, Grok, another candidate, or another local run.

Canonical entry points need the small shared scope-identity check necessary to reject a manifest that disagrees with their own loaded bytes, sibling closure, project or caller contract before unsafe effects. No arbitrary command-dispatch framework is approved. The supported scoped path cannot accept a new sink with an old claim, old generated caller, missing sibling, forged manifest, stale C or an unpinned externally loaded module. A manifest alone cannot prove what prompt the Host read: Host's caller-load receipt is independently required. Do not claim old global scripts can detect all new mixed invocation mistakes; keep them out of this scoped invocation.

The bundle remains in MAIN when the run folder is archived or its worktree removed. Its binding follows the same legitimate archived claim, not a newly fabricated active claim. Before every resumed lifecycle operation, including after compact, Host reloads the exact scoped caller and verifies the same manifest, candidate and reached-state receipts. The existing global compact hook remains unchanged; its generic instruction to reload installed Next/Finalization is not evidence that this bundle was reloaded. Producer integration must prove the explicit recovery route; if caller identity is lost, hold the next mutation and re-read it. Do not continue with the old global Finalization or watcher by convenience.

Unrelated runs, other repositories, and invocations without explicit scope retain their existing helper selection. Preserve all global config/hooks/cache/skills bytes and unrelated project helper bytes. There is no automatic watch sweep: the scoped watcher must enforce project `issue-143` on both live and archived lanes and must not reconcile unrelated runs.

## 6. Readiness and independent positive/negative discrimination

Independent test custody owns new acceptance meaning. Production may supply the implementation and mechanical generated manifests; it may not weaken tests or recast a failure as accepted semantics. Host must first adjudicate and integrate the independent #1113 delivery, then freeze final producer C containing the lifecycle repair **and** scoped mechanism, generated mirrors, documentation and accepted tests. Earlier first-diff and `193abb2e` watcher evidence remain unaccepted here. Prior green chains do not cover new mechanism bytes.

Required producer evidence before any real consumer install:

- Focused installer/resolver/render/script-sync suites, the integration walkthrough, and all applicable unwaived producer chains bound to final C. Independently exercise the assembled project payload, not only root-source imports. Record source tree, dirty scope, child processes/argv/cwd, complete loaded-module paths/hashes, raw outputs/exits and pre/post artifact identities. Mutation invalidates affected evidence.
- Positive: exact singleton #143-shaped live state; MAIN and linked-worktree starts resolve one caller/helper closure; idempotent install; explicit caller selection and compact/resume re-read; supported future intent recording; finalize/archive/PR retry; scoped live/archive watcher; retained bundle after worktree removal; bytes and legitimate ledger/claim/evidence custody preserved. Test against isolated fixtures, never by destructive dry-run of real #143.
- Negative installation: stale or missing QA/acceptance binding, same version/different C, dirty source substitution, wrong repo/main/common-dir/claim/issue/branch/worktree, forged/incomplete/mixed payload, old caller/new helper and inverse, missing dependency, traversal/symlink/foreign destination, interrupted install, changed owned file at removal, unsupported runtime/forge/bundle. Refusal has no consumer-state/global writes and no global fallback.
- Positive default discrimination: with no opt-in, existing resolver order and normal close behavior remain identical; unrelated co-active runs and preexisting project helpers remain byte-identical. Scope attempt from another run refuses without changing that run's default installation. Include consumer without package.json and cwd changed after resolution.
- Lifecycle discrimination remains the original #1113 contract: explicit unambiguous singleton versus malformed/missing/duplicate/conflicting identity and unsupported bundles; no closing text or forge linkage, including qualified references and commit-message hazards; request-only even with `pr_auto_merge: true`; no close-mode PR adoption; wrong head/base and closed-unmerged refusal; OPEN reuse/MERGED no-republish; actual OPEN intentionally kept-open, CLOSED violation, unavailable observation unknown. Exercise both watcher lanes before archive/cleanup effects, safe retries, unrelated-state preservation and legacy merge artifact rejection. This list adds no reinterpretation of the independent tests already in custody.

Host acceptance must name final C, actual rendered/packaged identities, independently accepted evidence and all remaining limitations. It cannot be replaced by this design approval, a version string, a worker's REPORT, unit-only fixtures, or the old producer chain receipt. Material source manifests, raw receipts, reports and failures must land in provider MAIN cache and be mirrored byte-for-byte into consumer MAIN #143 cache as produced by their authorized owners; a later copy must be labeled retrospective. ## 7. Actual #143 adoption, rollback and lifecycle separation

After exact producer acceptance, Host rechecks the real consumer's state/claim/worktree/root and immutable ledger against the installation binding without running finalize, watch, audit repair, sink or destructive `--check`/dry-run as a probe. A separately proven side-effect-free inspector may read the real state; fixture integration exercises mutations on isolated copies. Do not silently copy the MAIN ledger into the real worktree. Inventory all material MAIN evidence, including independent and provider mirrors, before eventual archive.

Then, and only then, Host may use the newly shipped supported install operation for this one target. Verify source-to-installed bytes, loaded generated caller provenance and every resolved helper, plus unchanged global and unrelated-helper canaries. Missing real intent fields are an expected **not-yet-ready lifecycle finding**, not an installer repair opportunity. Host must later record the already-authorized disposition through the supported lifecycle preparation, uniquely preserving all identity fields: `sink: pr`, `issue_action: comment_keep_open`, `keep_open_pr: explicit_singleton`, exactly issue 143. The supported caller passes the corresponding explicit mode to sink-pr. No offline placeholder or dummy publication proves compatibility.

Rollback before lifecycle use removes only unchanged manifest-owned local bundle bytes; conflicting or foreign bytes are preserved and reported. There is no global pointer to restore and no previous helper overwritten. Another accepted candidate goes to a separate immutable directory, and Host explicitly selects it; do not swap an in-use directory. Once new-format state or a durable request exists, removal/downgrade that would hand it to incompatible global code must refuse. Keep the matched bundle and resume forward, or require separately proven compatible successor handling. Never reconstruct an old claim, erase intent/request receipts, overwrite evidence, auto-reopen, close an issue, delete a request, force-push or rewrite history to roll back installation.

Installation is not GPU acceptance, archive readiness, request publication, merge permission or a terminal run verdict. The original #143 exact-candidate CPU/GPU/documentation contract still applies. A created/reused PR is request publication only; the issue stays OPEN, with mainline publication pending until separately authorized verified merge. Host retains every real lifecycle action and the provider mission's eventual outcome.
